topic.title: What the Editor Needs to Tell the Indexer

body.p: Scope of work Once the editor chooses a shortlist of potential indexers, negotiations can begin. First, the indexer’s availability and suitability need to be determined. Then fees and deadlines need to be set.

section.title: Scope of Work
section.p: Text density The editor should provide the indexer with as much information as possible about the project: the subject matter, its complexity, the intended audience, the length of the text, and any special requirements such as multiple indexes or embedded indexing.

section.title: Style Guidelines
section.p: Style guidelines Any specific style requirements should be communicated to the indexer before work begins. This includes the preferred style guide, any deviations from standard practice, and any publisher-specific conventions.

section.title: Negotiating the Fee
section.p: Fee arrangements Per-page rates Per-entry rates Per-hour rates Flat fee arrangements Indexing fees are typically structured in one of four ways: per-page, per-entry, per-hour, or flat fee. Per-page rates are the most common. The appropriate rate depends on the complexity of the material, the required turnaround time, and the indexer’s experience.

Cancellation fees Rush fees Special costs Special circumstances may warrant additional fees. Rush jobs typically incur a surcharge. Cancellation fees compensate the indexer for time reserved for the project. Other special costs may include shipping or software licensing.

section.title: Setting Deadlines
section.p: Deadlines Production schedule Deadlines should be realistic and take into account the complexity and length of the text. A common rule of thumb is that an indexer can complete 10–15 pages per hour for straightforward material. Complex or technical texts may require more time.

section.title: Embedded Indexing
section.p: Embedded indexingconsiderations If the publisher requires embedded indexing (where tags are inserted directly into the source files), this affects both the choice of indexer and the fee, as not all indexers have experience with embedded indexing software.
